152144.title: Portrait of Anne of Austria (1601-1666), Queen of France
152144.creator: workshop of Peter Paul Rubens

editorial.note: School of Peter Paul Rubens (1577 - 1640). Portrait of Anne of Austria, c. 1622. Every detail of this portrait of Anne of Austria radiates power and importance. The woman is wearing a richly decorated gown embroidered in gold.

152155.title: Portrait of Catharina van der Voort
152155.creator: Abraham van den Tempel

editorial.note: Catharina’s wealth radiates from this portrait. Van den Tempel positioned her before a balustrade, near a rosebush.

152231.title: Portrait of Anne of Hanover, Princess Royal and Princess of Orange, Consort of Prince William IV
152231.creator: attributed to Johann Valentin Tischbein

editorial.note: Anna of Hannover, attributed to J.V. Tischbein, 1753. Princess Anna was the eldest daughter of George II of England. In 1734 she married William IV.
Hortense de Beauharnais became the first queen of Holland in 1806 when her husband Louis Napoleon ascended the throne. In this portrait, she wears a tiara adorned with pearls, a royal jewel.

152479.title: Portrait of Charlotta Beatrix Strick van Linschoten
152479.creator: Mattheus Verheyden

editorial.note: Strick van Linschoten had herself portrayed in a gown adorned with golden and brightly coloured flowers. Behind her is a country estate, probably Eemwijck, located opposite Essesteijn, before which her husband poses.

152559.title: Portrait of Jeanne-Elisabeth Sellon, Lady Tyrell
152559.creator: Jean-Etienne Liotard

editorial.note: Like Liotard himself, Jeanne-Elisabeth Sellon was born in Geneva to Huguenot parents, who had been forced to flee France in 1685. She married an English baronet, Sir Charles Tyrell, in 1726.
